---
title: "PROC TABULATE"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Show an HTML document of sas_html() in an isolated frame, so its style
# sheet does not mix with the page.
show_html <- function(doc, height = 320) {
  esc <- gsub('"', "&quot;", gsub("&", "&amp;", doc, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf(
    '<iframe srcdoc="%s" style="width: 100%%; height: %dpx; border: 1px solid #c1c1c1;"></iframe>',
    esc, height))
}
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

PROC TABULATE builds a table from CLASS and VAR variables and a TABLE
statement: the page, row and column dimensions, crossed with `*`, concatenated
with blanks, and `ALL` for totals. sasonr writes the table in the listing with
its box lines, as an ODS table, and in the HTML or RTF document.

```{r}
prog <- "
options nocenter;
data trial;
  input arm $ sex $ age;
  datalines;
A F 34
A M 41
A F 29
B M 52
B F 47
B M 38
;
run;
"
```

## Counts by two classes

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc tabulate data=trial;
  class arm sex;
  table sex all, arm*n;
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## Statistics of an analysis variable

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc tabulate data=trial;
  class arm;
  var age;
  table arm all, age*(n mean min max);
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## The HTML output

The same table as an HTML document, from `sas_html()`:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show_html(sas_html(res), height = 300)
```

## PROC TABULATE as an R call

The translation writes the step as one call of `sas_proc_tabulate()`: CLASS
and VAR are variable names, the TABLE statement is marked with
`sas_tabulate_table()` (its dimensions are SAS syntax).

```{r}
cat(tail(as.character(sas_script(res)), 3), sep = "\n")
```

```{r}
s <- sas_session()
invisible(sas_run(prog, session = s))
s |> sas_proc_tabulate(data = "trial", class = c(arm, sex), table = sas_tabulate_table("sex all, arm*n"))
cat(sas_listing(s), sep = "\n")
```

## On a data frame

`sas_tabulate_df()` takes the same arguments with a data frame.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(arm = c("A", "A", "B"), age = c(34, 41, 52))
as.data.frame(sas_tabulate_df(df, class = arm, var = age, table = sas_tabulate_table("arm all, age*(n mean)")))
```
